question: Spike planted A Site Haven, 3v3, 28s. You're Viper (2 Snake Bites, wall already placed on site). DEF will retake from CT/A Link and A Long. How do you hold post-plant?

options.label: Save both Snake Bites on lineups for the spike and hold 3 attackers in crossfire at A Short, A Long, and Link
options.explication_courte: Your Toxic Screen already splits the site; saving mollys for the defuse moment plus a 3-angle crossfire covers every retake axis in a 3v3.

options.label: Drop one Snake Bite onto the spike immediately to deny an early defuse, keep the second in reserve
options.explication_courte: Denying the early defuse works if defenders push fast, but spending a molly before contact can waste it if the retake is slow; keeping at least one in reserve is still correct play.

sources_option.citation: Use utility reactively; layer it rather than spending every tool immediately after planting, or defenders wait it out and retake with full time.

options.label: Cluster all 3 attackers behind Viper's wall near the spike for concentrated fire on the main retake axis
options.explication_courte: Grouping 3 bodies concentrates fire but leaves 2 of the 3 retake axes uncovered; a Link+Long split lets DEF take the site from behind while you're focused on one angle.

sources_option.citation: Spread out and play off the spike; grouping your bodies leaves other approach lines open for a split retake to punish.

options.label: Dump the wall + both Snake Bites all at once before the retake, then fall back without holding any angle
options.explication_courte: Burning all util before any contact lets DEF wait it out and retake a site with no util and no angles held; the post-plant is lost by waste.

sources_option.citation: Dumping all utility pre-contact concedes the tempo; defenders re-time the retake once the util fades and you hold nothing.

explication_longue:
Situation: 3v3 post-plant on A Site Haven, 28 seconds, spike planted. You're Viper: your Toxic Screen (wall) is already placed splitting the site, you have 2 Snake Bites left. The 3 defenders will retake from CT/A Link and A Long.

Post-plant with a 3v3 requires covering every retake axis with the right number of bodies and holding delay util for when the defuse actually starts. Haven A has three defender approach lines (A Short/CT, A Link, A Long) — three attackers must occupy three distinct angles, never stack. The Viper wall helps by cutting vision on one axis, reducing the problem to two live lines to hold.

The optimal line saves both Snake Bites on lineups targeting the defuse spot: activate on the defuse sound, forcing DEF to clear the molly (wasted time) before touching the spike. Meanwhile, the 3-angle crossfire punishes any exposure. Denying the defuse too early (acceptable option) works if the retake is fast, but risks wasting a molly; clustering bodies (costly) leaves an axis open to a split push.

Estimated elite distribution: ~55% save mollys on lineups + 3-angle crossfire, ~20% early deny with one reserve, ~18% cluster bodies (costly), ~5% dump all util before contact (the mistake). GTO tolerance: any line that keeps at least one molly for the defuse AND covers more than one axis is acceptable.

sources.citation: Molly lineups on the spike are the go-to post-plant tool; holding them until the defuse begins is what eats the enemies' time.
Spread out (not all same spot), play off the spike, hold crossfires, and use utility to delay the defuse.
Viper's wall and molly lineups are a core ranked post-plant win condition; the wall splits the site and the mollys deny the defuse spot.

_gaps.incertitude: Estimations depuis guides post-plant et lineups Viper (nonagames, dignitas, cheatspulse) ; la repartition depend fortement de la maitrise des lineups Viper et de la comp adverse (agents flash/recon) non specifiee.
On suppose le Toxic Screen deja pose (fuel a moitie) ; l'etat exact du fuel Viper influe sur la capacite a re-scinder le site et n'est pas encode dans le schema.
Les 3 DEF sont supposes retaker de Link+Long+CT mais aucune position n'est confirmee ; un juge pourrait juger la ligne optimale differente si les DEF stackent un seul axe.
